newsitem.title: UK: Russia to export new supersonic missile - Jane's.
newsitem.headline: Russia to export new supersonic missile - Jane's.

text.p: Russia is poised to export to the Middle and Far East a deadly new supersonic anti-ship missile that travels at two-and-a-half times the speed of sound, Jane's Defence Weekly said on Thursday.
"They have come up with a pretty impressive weapon that will be very difficult to shoot down," said Mark Daly, editor of the respected defence magazine.
The Yakhont, which means gem in Russian, has a range of up to 300 kilometres and can be fired from ships and submarines.
It has a far greater range than the French-built Exocet which, like the American Tomahawk and Harpoon missiles, is subsonic.
"The Yakhont is a lot harder to shoot down than the Exocet. It is powered by a ram jet and is hard to detect as well as to shoot down," Daly said.
The magazine said it was given exclusive access by NPO Mashinostroeniya officials and allowed close inspection of a full-scale mock-up of the Yakhont, which is now being prepared for export.
The Russian officials said they believed the total size of the anti-ship missile market up to 2005 will total between $10-12 billion.
They saw the Middle East and Far East as the greatest potential markets for the new weapon but refused to be specific on which countries might finally purchase it.
The Yakhont is due to appear on the market in the next two to three years, the officials told Jane's.
The 8.9 metre-long missile is being built in submarine, ship and coastal battery-launched variants. An air-deployed version with a launch weight of 2.5 tonnes is in development, officials revealed.
